It should be incredibly obvious how I know this.

Going through with the sale of my fathers house when he was in a chemically induced coma after a major stroke, leaving my little brother homeless.

I knew I had to, because he had already initiated the sale, and the place would have made his life incredibly difficult if he was going to survive at all. I also couldn't let my little brother get stuck there. He would never have been able to get a place of his own from the guilt of abandoning his father.

It worked out incredibly well under the circumstances. My father survived, spent months in the hospital, got him a new place he could handle in a wheelchair, and my little brother found a place of his own.

Man, it would have been so easy to give in to the fear and guilt of getting it wrong, but I think I was numb enough from the grief that it was just barely doable.

Making big choices that affect other people is so hard. You don't want to screw anyone over and often feel like you can't fully understand their positions to make the best choice for them. I feel you and am really happy it worked out. Good job sticking to the right thing even though it was tough!

What university program to go into. Going to University was an non-negotiable requirement in my family. I had never really enjoyed school to be honest and couldn't imagine what job I wanted to get and therefore what I should study. I ended up choosing computer science as that was one of my least hated classes in high school although parts of it were still annoying. Turns out in University comp sci is very different from what it was in high school and entails a lot of really difficult and abstract math and not as much actual fun programming. I ended up dropping out after a few rough years.

Re-thought the whole thing and came to the conclusion that I had been neglecting my creative side since elementary school and did a fine art portfolio program for the hell of it. I liked it okay and decided to use the portfolio I had made to try to get into a fine arts bachelor program. Succeeded and went to art school for a few years. Discovered that I also hated all the bullshit in the art world and a lot of the people in the art world, and ended up being forced by program restrictions to take a bunch of courses I didn't care for in order to get the degree I needed to do anything in the art world. Thought about it some more, realized I didn't think I could stomach a life of interacting with "art people" anyway and dropped out of that program too.

Now I'm a busboy at a restaurant. I wouldn't say I'm happy, but I have very little responsibility, get by on what I make and get to come home everyday and play videogames to my heart's content. I still have no idea what the fuck to do with my life and I'm pretty sure I'm wasting it by not being more ambitious and motivated but I just don't give a shit anymore. Pretty sure there is no job that I would enjoy, it's just a question of having extra money or not and having more money to buy stupid shit has never really made me happy either anyway so fuck it.

Only thing I'd advise you to think about is retirement. Even if buying stuff doesn't give you satisfaction (same boat here), you don't want to have to work until you die to avoid crushing poverty. Find something you can tolerate that makes enough for you to save in addition to consuming.

Picking something to do for the rest of your life is really hard. I can see why you've washed out twice.

Whether to move to a different country after graduation for a new job.

I was dating a pretty amazing girl at the time whom I honestly could picture myself marrying. We had been dating a few months in perfect bliss until I received the news of getting a full job offer at the end of an internship. The opportunity would require me to move to a different country on a permanent basis for the foreseeable future.

She couldn't follow me there as she had moved to my present city to pursue her own dream and was locked into at least another 3 years after which she could only practice in my home country. In the 8 months that followed from the offer and my acceptance, we tried to date but the stress of it coming on was too much for the relationship to bear.

Making that choice to take this opportunity was the hardest one I've ever had to do and I still don't know if it was the right thing. I think if I passed it up for her I would have resented it my whole life. Only time will tell I suppose.

Keeping my son when I was pregnant at 19 from a one night stand. How could I take care of a baby when I was a kid myself? Is my life over now? Losing friends because you can no longer go party and my life was so different with a newborn, doing it all by myself without any help, etc etc)

hardest decision I ever made but easily, hands down, the very best decision for me.

It can be a lot of work having kids young. But as a parent, I understand why you feel it was the right choice now. They make you life so much more satisfying and bring so much joy. It can also really make you step up and get your life together since someone you love is depending on you.

I'm really glad it worked out well for you and I hope you and your baby are really happy. Did the negatives end up being as bad as you'd worried at the time?

I had no idea I could love anything that fiercely. Nothing prepares you for that kind of love. Negatives sucked. They were horrible. But nowhere near as bad as the fears in my head built them up to be. Some of the negatives were pretty bad, but they were made bearable by the notion of the alternative: not having my son and that was inconceivable to me. I used to think about how close I came to not having him and it would make me burst out in tears at the sheer horror of that thought. Everything else compared to that was relative and survivable. If I was given the opportunity to not have him at 19 but wait until I was older.....I wouldn't. It was hard....so damn hard...but worth every single minute.

My baby is now a strapping 22 year old going to school. It has been a helluva ride :)

edit: I'd like to add that my post has nothing to do with "pro life" or "pro choice"..or one decision being better or more right than the other. For me, keeping my son was the best decision. Others make different choices. They are all hard choices in this area that we make doing the very best that we can.

Leaving my cat with my parents halfway across the country while I was going through a tough spot. I thought it would be better because I could barely afford anything extra, let alone the better food that my cat needed.

Turns out that it was a really bad decision. We learned that having a cat, especially this cat, helps my stress & anxiety levels immensely, that my daughter is extremely attached to the furball (she cried every night for a week), and my cat has separation anxiety. My dad moved in with me to help out about a month after I left the cat with them and stayed until I was on my feet again.

It may not seem like a huge decision for most people, but I'd had my cat for 5 years at that point and he is like a second child to me. While his separation anxiety is a little better, he still gets too stressed for me to be gone overnight, so he comes with us on vacation. Thankfully he loves car rides.

If you often visit this sub, you have probably heard of Treasure Trooper (Ref / Non-ref).

This site is available to residents of the US, Canada and the UK. Treasure Trooper pays out to Paypal or by check in the mail. You are paid automatically once a month if you reach $20. If you want, you can request an instant payout at $20 (there is a 50 cent fee for instant payout).

The site is massive and a little confusing at times. There are multiple currencies in the site:

  • Cash - Paypal, Check

  • Platinum Coins - can be traded for gift cards to amazon (1 platinum coin is $1), these can also be used to trade in for prizes like iPods and Wii U's.

  • Gold Coin - Used for the slot machine or the treasure hunt

  • Arrowhead - Worth one penny, 100 can be traded in for a platinum coin

  • Dragon Scale - Pretty worthless, used in dragon minigame

  • Pearl - Trade in 8 of these to buy a referral, found in daily game

Now, the part you all have been waiting for. This is how I make $20 a month without too much effort. I usually only go for activities that pay Cash. There are plenty of mini games and activities that reward you with other currency, which is usually not as valuable as cash. These activities are found under the Earn tab.

  • Cash Calls - This is a very nice way to earn a lot of money. Most of the offers require you to be on the line with a company for 4 minutes and then you get paid (usually $3-4). If you aren't comfortable with speaking to people, you can usually stall time with the robot voice and still get paid just fine. These usually get replaced throughout the month, but a completely new set is present at the beginning of every month. Unfortunately, you need to have earned a minimum of $5 on offers and surveys before you are eligible for these.

  • Cash Offers - This is where most of my earning is done. This includes activities like signing up for a website and confirming your email and getting paid $.50. Treasure Trooper shows you which ones are the most popular, and I usually go off of that to earn my money.

  • Daily Surveys - Every day, there are 8 daily surveys which can each be done once a day. I don't usually do surveys, but if you qualify for most of them then you can earn a good deal of money.

  • Survey Seeker - Finds surveys that fit you better so you don't get disqualified as much. These often double check your information so make sure you are putting honest information (or easy to remember fake information).

  • Cash Tasks - These are tasks similar to mturk, but they pay a lot less.

  • Cash Search - Treasure Trooper Search engine, not worth it

  • Cash Shopping - Cash back on purchases, lose money instead of make it

  • Cash Videos - This is like PerkTV, but it pays a whole lot less

  • Cash Radio - Pays out in arrowheads (worth $.01 each), makes you enter a captcha every 10 minutes. Overall, not really worth it.

  • Daily Poll - Get paid 2 arrowheads to answer a poll

Treasure Hunt - This is a ploy that treasure trooper uses to get you to spend money on treasure maps which can be put together so that you can find a hidden treasure worth $100. A lot of the stuff on the website is to try to get you to not cash out, but if you focus on the right things, you should have no problem earning $20 a month.

I earn my money from doing a couple of easy cash offers a day. Couple this with a survey a day and you should have no problem reaching or even exceeding $20 a month. I hope you all enjoy the site and if you have any questions, feel free to ask me!
